skill.name: email
skill.description: Provides local shell scripts for IMAP and SMTP email operations, including sending messages, listing recent mail, and reading message content. Credentials are read from macOS Keychain.
skill.summary: Send, fetch, and read email through IMAP and SMTP using local shell scripts and macOS Keychain credentials.
skill.author: 7Sageer, Claude

security_audit.summary: The skill has legitimate IMAP and SMTP functionality, but it also reads macOS Keychain credentials and can send email from a configured account. I confirmed the sensitive credential access and actual send/read behavior, dismissed many Markdown and benign shell redirection false positives, and added semantic findings for personal account data, missing send confirmation, and account-specific mailbox scraping.

remediation.issue: Personal mailbox details are included as default configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the SUSTech account, real email address, display name, and local user paths with neutral placeholders before publication.

remediation.issue: The send script does not enforce confirmation before SMTP upload.
remediation.suggestion: Add a required dry-run or explicit confirmation flag before any email is sent, and make agents show recipient, subject, and body first.

remediation.issue: Keychain password retrieval is both executable behavior and documented as a password display command.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid instructions that print passwords, use app-specific credentials, and document the exact limited Keychain services the scripts may access.

remediation.issue: A helper script performs account-specific mailbox search and message reading.
remediation.suggestion: Remove search-mail.sh or convert it into a generic, user-scoped search tool that requires explicit account, query, and message range inputs.

remediation.issue: Mailbox, count, email ID, and address inputs receive limited validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate numeric ranges, mailbox names, and recipient addresses before passing values to curl or IMAP requests.

semantic_findings.title: Hard-Coded Personal Mail Account
semantic_findings.description: The skill ships SUSTech as the default account with a real mailbox address and display name. This exposes a personal identity and may cause agents to act against the author account if matching Keychain credentials exist.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The account file, skill documentation, and manual all contain the same real mailbox identity and make it the default account. This is direct evidence of user-specific configuration in a public skill.

semantic_findings.title: Email Sending Lacks Enforced Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: send-email.sh sends immediately once recipient, subject, and body arguments are present. The skill documentation advises confirmation, but the script does not enforce a confirmation or dry-run step before SMTP upload.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script validates only required arguments before calling curl to send the message. The only confirmation requirement appears in documentation, so enforcement depends on the agent behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Account-Specific Mailbox Search Helper
semantic_findings.description: search-mail.sh searches a hard-coded SUSTech mailbox range for physical fitness related terms and prints matching messages. This is a private, account-specific mailbox scrape rather than a generic marketplace workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script contains a fixed message ID range, fixed account name, and narrow Chinese search terms, then reads matching messages. That combination strongly indicates a personal mailbox automation artifact.

content.value_statement: AI agents often need structured access to email without opening a full mail client. This skill provides script-based IMAP and SMTP workflows for reading, listing, and sending messages.
actual_capabilities: Sends plain text email through SMTP using configured account credentials.
Fetches recent message headers from an IMAP mailbox.
Reads a specific email by message ID in summary, full, headers, or body format.
Uses macOS Keychain service entries for IMAP and SMTP passwords.
Supports account, mailbox, count, recipient, subject, body, and CC options.
limitations: Requires macOS Keychain and local shell access.
Does not implement OAuth2 or modern provider-specific authentication flows.
Does not handle attachments or rich HTML message composition.
Includes user-specific default account settings that should be replaced before use.

use_cases.title: Check Recent Inbox Activity
use_cases.description: List the latest messages with sender, subject, date, and read status for quick triage.

use_cases.title: Send Operational Updates
use_cases.description: Send concise plain text notifications from a configured mailbox after details are confirmed.

use_cases.title: Read Message Context
use_cases.description: Retrieve a selected message so an assistant can summarize or extract key details.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Inbox
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my default inbox and summarize the five most recent emails with sender, subject, and date.

prompt_templates.title: Read One Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Read email number 12 from my inbox and give me a short summary with any requested action.

prompt_templates.title: Draft and Send Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Send a plain text email to Alex about the project status after showing me the recipient, subject, and body for confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Triage a Mailbox Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the latest 20 messages in my Sent folder, identify follow-up items, and read only the messages needed for context.

output_examples.output: A short inbox summary with five entries, each showing message number, sender, subject, date, and read status.

output_examples.input: Read email number 42 as a summary.
output_examples.output: A concise message view with sender, date, subject, and a preview of the message body.
A confirmation-ready message containing the selected recipient, subject, and plain text body before sending.

best_practices: Replace all sample account values with your own placeholders before publishing or sharing.
Require explicit user confirmation before any message is sent.
Use app-specific passwords or limited-scope credentials when the provider supports them.
anti_patterns: Do not publish a skill with a real personal mailbox as the default account.
Do not ask an assistant to print Keychain passwords into chat or logs.
Do not run broad mailbox searches unless the user requested the exact scope.

faq.question: Can this skill send email?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses SMTP through curl and the configured account credentials.

faq.question: Where are passwords stored?
faq.answer: The scripts read passwords from macOS Keychain service entries.

faq.question: Does it support Gmail or Outlook?
faq.answer: It documents IMAP and SMTP settings, but modern OAuth flows are not implemented.

faq.question: Can it read full email bodies?
faq.answer: Yes. The read script can output a summary, headers, body, or full message.

faq.question: Does it process attachments?
faq.answer: No. Attachment handling is listed as a future enhancement.

faq.question: Is it ready for public marketplace use?
faq.answer: Not without changes. Personal account details and risky email actions need safer defaults.
